verdict.rationale: Blaxel ships isolated cloud sandboxes for code execution. Agents can create and operate them through an MCP server, fork them from snapshots for safe experimentation, and restrict outbound traffic with domain allowlists that prevent data exfiltration. This is genuine sandbox isolation rather than a dry-run mode. However, the docs never explicitly state that sandbox testing is separated from production data, for example through a test/production environment split or a data-isolation guarantee. missing for 10: explicit documentation of separation from production data or environments, independent or hands-on corroboration of isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Every Blaxel sandbox exposes a built-in MCP server so agents can operate the sandbox using tool calls for files, processes, ports, and previews.
Create point-in-time snapshots of sandboxes, roll them back to a checkpoint, and fork them into new sandboxes.
Restrict which external domains, HTTP methods, and URL paths a Blaxel sandbox can reach using allowlists and denylists to prevent data exfiltration and unwanted outbound traffic.
Scope everything a sandbox runs on your behalf to an unprivileged user while the sandbox API keeps the privileges it needs.
